strongestClocks.title: Children’s Digital Identity and Age-Gating Clock
strongestClocks.signals: Tracks the rapid conversion of child-online-safety policy into mandatory age assurance, account restrictions, parental-authorisation systems, biometric or document-based age estimation and reusable proof-of-age infrastructure. Current evidence includes an Australian under-16 restriction in force, UK age assurance operating at scale, French digital-majority legislation and an EU verification app designed for national rollout and European Digital Identity Wallet compatibility.

strongestClocks.raiseRule: Raise when age assurance becomes legally required across major services, expands across jurisdictions, relies on biometric or government-identity onboarding, becomes interoperable with general identity wallets, creates persistent records or gates lawful adult access.
strongestClocks.lowerRule: Lower when anonymous or selective-disclosure proof-of-age methods, data minimisation, non-identity alternatives, deletion rights, independent audits and meaningful appeal rights are legally enforceable and practically available.

latestDrops.title: Australia's under-16 social-media account restriction is in force
latestDrops.summary: From 10 December 2025, age-restricted social-media platforms must take reasonable steps to prevent Australians under 16 from creating or keeping accounts. The regulator reports continuing compliance monitoring.
latestDrops.evidenceLevel: Official regulator · law in force · active compliance
latestDrops.identityLink: Platforms must operate age-assurance systems, while privacy restrictions and platform responsibility remain part of the legal design.
latestDrops.claimBoundary: This proves mandatory age restriction and age-assurance deployment in Australia. It does not prove that the stated child-safety purpose is a covert digital-ID plan.

latestDrops.title: Australia updates the platform definition used by its social-media minimum-age law
latestDrops.summary: Australia updated the rules in March 2026 to focus the minimum-age obligation on account-based recommender systems and design features such as endless feeds, feedback signals and time-limited content.
latestDrops.evidenceLevel: Official government · implementing rules updated
latestDrops.identityLink: The regulated scope determines where platforms must deploy account-age controls.
latestDrops.claimBoundary: The update demonstrates continuing implementation, not a finding about hidden motive.

latestDrops.title: UK age checks are deployed at unprecedented scale under the Online Safety Act
latestDrops.summary: Ofcom's July 2026 statutory report states that many services are required to use highly effective age assurance and that age checks have been deployed at unprecedented scale.
latestDrops.evidenceLevel: Official regulator · statutory report · active enforcement
latestDrops.identityLink: Regulated services must determine whether users meet age thresholds using highly effective age assurance.
latestDrops.claimBoundary: This proves large-scale age assurance. It does not establish that every service must collect a government identity document or that a single universal identity database exists.

latestDrops.title: EU urges Member States to make a common age-verification app available by the end of 2026
latestDrops.summary: The European Commission adopted a recommendation on 29 April 2026 urging Member States to accelerate rollout of the EU age-verification app. The app may operate independently or be integrated into a European Digital Identity Wallet.
latestDrops.evidenceLevel: Official EU recommendation · deployment deadline
latestDrops.identityLink: The Commission explicitly permits integration with European Digital Identity Wallet infrastructure.
latestDrops.claimBoundary: Wallet compatibility is documented infrastructure convergence. It does not prove that child safety is merely a cover or that the wallet will become compulsory for all online activity.

latestDrops.title: EU age-verification blueprint is technically ready and supports national eIDs, passports and identity cards
latestDrops.summary: The Commission says its age-verification solution became feature-ready in April 2026. Proof of age can be issued from national eIDs, passports, identity cards, banking apps or offline activation, while the design aims to disclose only the required age threshold.
latestDrops.evidenceLevel: Official EU technical blueprint · implementation-ready
latestDrops.identityLink: The proof can be bootstrapped from government identity documents, national eIDs or trusted applications, while using selective disclosure and zero-knowledge techniques.
latestDrops.claimBoundary: The identity-document onboarding route is documented. The privacy-preserving design is also documented and must be included as counter-evidence against claims of inevitable centralised identity tracking.

latestDrops.title: Denmark, France, Greece, Italy and Spain are adopting customised versions of the EU age-verification solution
latestDrops.summary: The Commission identifies five Member States taking up the common technical solution with a view to publishing customised national age-verification applications.
latestDrops.evidenceLevel: Official EU rollout record · multi-jurisdiction adoption
latestDrops.identityLink: The national apps use a harmonised proof-of-age architecture designed to interoperate with European identity-wallet standards.
latestDrops.claimBoundary: Common architecture across several countries proves policy and technical convergence, not a secret unified identity mandate.

latestDrops.title: France enacted a digital-majority framework requiring parental consent below 15 and technical verification
latestDrops.summary: France's digital-majority law requires social-network providers to refuse registration by children under 15 without parental consent and provides for certified technical solutions to verify age and parental authorisation, subject to implementation and European-law constraints.
latestDrops.evidenceLevel: Official legislation · enacted framework
latestDrops.identityLink: The law expressly requires technical age and parental-authorisation verification mechanisms.
latestDrops.claimBoundary: The statute is real, but practical enforcement and compatibility with EU law must be tracked separately from the enacted text.

latestDrops.title: EU protection-of-minors guidelines and age-verification prototype establish a common DSA implementation route
latestDrops.summary: The European Commission issued protection-of-minors guidelines and an age-verification prototype under the Digital Services Act, creating a common compliance and technical route for platforms operating across the EU.
latestDrops.evidenceLevel: Official EU regulatory guidance · technical prototype
latestDrops.identityLink: The common prototype provides reusable proof-of-age infrastructure for platform compliance.
latestDrops.claimBoundary: The DSA route establishes common compliance expectations but the guidelines themselves do not prove a universal compulsory identity system.

latestDrops.summary: Australia updated the rules in March 2026 to focus the minimum-age obligation on account-based recommender systems and design features such as endless feeds, feedback signals and time-limited content.
latestDrops.evidenceLevel: Official government · implementing rules updated
latestDrops.identityLink: The regulated scope determines where platforms must deploy account-age controls.
latestDrops.claimBoundary: The update demonstrates continuing implementation, not a finding about hidden motive.

latestDrops.title: UK age checks are deployed at unprecedented scale under the Online Safety Act
latestDrops.summary: Ofcom's July 2026 statutory report states that many services are required to use highly effective age assurance and that age checks have been deployed at unprecedented scale.
latestDrops.evidenceLevel: Official regulator · statutory report · active enforcement
latestDrops.identityLink: Regulated services must determine whether users meet age thresholds using highly effective age assurance.
latestDrops.claimBoundary: This proves large-scale age assurance. It does not establish that every service must collect a government identity document or that a single universal identity database exists.

latestDrops.title: EU urges Member States to make a common age-verification app available by the end of 2026
latestDrops.summary: The European Commission adopted a recommendation on 29 April 2026 urging Member States to accelerate rollout of the EU age-verification app. The app may operate independently or be integrated into a European Digital Identity Wallet.
latestDrops.evidenceLevel: Official EU recommendation · deployment deadline
latestDrops.identityLink: The Commission explicitly permits integration with European Digital Identity Wallet infrastructure.
latestDrops.claimBoundary: Wallet compatibility is documented infrastructure convergence. It does not prove that child safety is merely a cover or that the wallet will become compulsory for all online activity.

latestDrops.title: EU age-verification blueprint is technically ready and supports national eIDs, passports and identity cards
latestDrops.summary: The Commission says its age-verification solution became feature-ready in April 2026. Proof of age can be issued from national eIDs, passports, identity cards, banking apps or offline activation, while the design aims to disclose only the required age threshold.
latestDrops.evidenceLevel: Official EU technical blueprint · implementation-ready
latestDrops.identityLink: The proof can be bootstrapped from government identity documents, national eIDs or trusted applications, while using selective disclosure and zero-knowledge techniques.
latestDrops.claimBoundary: The identity-document onboarding route is documented. The privacy-preserving design is also documented and must be included as counter-evidence against claims of inevitable centralised identity tracking.

latestDrops.title: Denmark, France, Greece, Italy and Spain are adopting customised versions of the EU age-verification solution
latestDrops.summary: The Commission identifies five Member States taking up the common technical solution with a view to publishing customised national age-verification applications.
latestDrops.evidenceLevel: Official EU rollout record · multi-jurisdiction adoption
latestDrops.identityLink: The national apps use a harmonised proof-of-age architecture designed to interoperate with European identity-wallet standards.
latestDrops.claimBoundary: Common architecture across several countries proves policy and technical convergence, not a secret unified identity mandate.

latestDrops.title: France enacted a digital-majority framework requiring parental consent below 15 and technical verification
latestDrops.summary: France's digital-majority law requires social-network providers to refuse registration by children under 15 without parental consent and provides for certified technical solutions to verify age and parental authorisation, subject to implementation and European-law constraints.
latestDrops.evidenceLevel: Official legislation · enacted framework
latestDrops.identityLink: The law expressly requires technical age and parental-authorisation verification mechanisms.
latestDrops.claimBoundary: The statute is real, but practical enforcement and compatibility with EU law must be tracked separately from the enacted text.

latestDrops.title: EU protection-of-minors guidelines and age-verification prototype establish a common DSA implementation route
latestDrops.summary: The European Commission issued protection-of-minors guidelines and an age-verification prototype under the Digital Services Act, creating a common compliance and technical route for platforms operating across the EU.
latestDrops.evidenceLevel: Official EU regulatory guidance · technical prototype
latestDrops.identityLink: The common prototype provides reusable proof-of-age infrastructure for platform compliance.
latestDrops.claimBoundary: The DSA route establishes common compliance expectations but the guidelines themselves do not prove a universal compulsory identity system.

latestDrops.title: Every EU Member State must make at least one European Digital Identity Wallet available by the end of 2026
latestDrops.summary: The European Commission says Member States will make wallets available to citizens, residents and businesses by the end of 2026. More than 550 companies and public authorities across 26 Member States and associated countries have participated in large-scale pilots.
latestDrops.evidenceLevel: Official EU implementation page · statutory rollout
latestDrops.identityLink: The wallet is designed for public and private services using common standards and interoperable person-identification data.
latestDrops.claimBoundary: Mandatory state provision and common standards are documented. Official policy says individual use is voluntary and selective disclosure is a core safeguard.

latestDrops.title: EU remote-onboarding standards for digital identity wallets entered implementing law in April 2026
latestDrops.summary: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/798 sets reference standards and specifications for remote onboarding to European Digital Identity Wallets at high assurance levels.
latestDrops.evidenceLevel: Official EU law · implementing regulation
latestDrops.identityLink: The regulation operationalises identity-wallet onboarding rather than leaving it at policy or pilot stage.
latestDrops.claimBoundary: This proves technical and legal implementation. It does not prove that all services will require the wallet.
